comments.author: mchusma
comments.why: Isaac Arthur's deep explanation of Fermi Paradox and Dyson sphere detectability
comments.text: If interested in this kind of thing, I always recommend Issac Arthur. He describes the Fermi Paradox and related concepts 100x better than anyone else. Some relevant ones: The Fermi Paradox Compendium [LINK] Fermi Paradox: The Dyson Dilemma v2.0 [VIDEO] I believe he would say that there is no really good explanation to why we don't see other intelligent civilizations except that we are effectively the first (at least in our galaxy), and intelligent space-faring life is exceedingly rare. This is a similar conclusion to Robin Hanson here, but I think I think Issac Arthur does a better job of deeply explaining it. I think both would agree though.

comments.why: Covers why hiding a Dyson sphere is implausible
comments.text: See [1] and [2] where the idea of hiding a Dyson sphere is covered in depth. It essentially means breaking the laws of thermodynamics, specifically entropy. Hit and object with light from a star and it heats up. It radiates away that heat in a predictable way. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
